# php2shell check — p2s.cheeserobot.org

Public checker for the patch & mitigation status of CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619
(PHP `session.upload_progress` use-after-free; "php2shell"). One URL at a time,
submitted at `/?url=<host>` or through the JSON API below.

## What it does

It probes a URL you name with a handful of INERT requests and reports which
defenses against CVE-2026-109618/619 are observable from the outside:

- a version banner check (X-Powered-By / Server headers vs. the patched
  release list: 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, 8.5.12),
- a multipart reachability test across POST/PUT/PATCH (urlencoded baseline +
  one text-field multipart per method — no file part, no upload-progress
  field, nothing exploit-shaped, never stalling),
- a session-fixation probe: one multipart POST whose first field is a random
  session id; if the response Set-Cookie adopts OUR id, the app accepts
  attacker-chosen session ids — the precondition the CVE chains build on.

## Verdicts

- PATCHED (green): a PHP version banner at or above a fixed release.
- UNPATCHED (red): a PHP version banner below a fixed release.
- BLOCKED (green): every multipart-family request is rejected by an edge
  rule (WAF/CDN) before a parser sees it.
- ASSUMED VULNERABLE (red): multipart requests reach the backend and no
  patched runtime could be confirmed — or the fixation probe was adopted.
- NO PHP DETECTED (green): nothing POST-shaped is processed and there are
  zero PHP indicators (no banner, no session cookie) — consistent with a
  static site; nothing to exploit at that URL.
- OFFLINE (green): the URL refuses connections; nothing is serving.
- UNKNOWN: anything not covered above (remote probing cannot see everything;
  the checker says so instead of over-claiming).

## Honest limits

- Results are best-effort indications from the OUTSIDE. NO GUARANTEES:
  banners can lie, caches can hide the origin, edges behave differently per
  route. This is NOT a vulnerability assessment — verify on the host.
- A CDN/WAF block only helps if the origin is not directly reachable.
- Edge-level and app-level rejections with the same status cannot be told
  apart remotely.
- The deeper exploit chains (var_destroy UAF, handler mismatch, filename→LFI)
  need host-side access or exploit-shaped traffic and are deliberately NOT
  tested by this service.

## API (JSON)

- GET  /api/health — liveness + build info.
- GET  /api/releases — the patched-release list used for version verdicts.
- GET  /api/pow?for=scan|status — proof-of-work challenge (single-use, TTL).
- POST /api/scan — body: {"url": "https://…", "level": "banner|block",
  "force": bool, "pow": {"id","nonce"}} → {"job_id"}; one URL per job.
- GET  /api/job/<id>?pow_id=…&pow_nonce=… — poll a job (needs its own PoW).
- GET  /api/og?url=<u> — 1200x630 PNG preview card of the stored result
  (read-only; never triggers a scan).
- GET  /llms.txt — this file.

Every scan submission and every poll must present a fresh proof-of-work
solution (browser-side ~1s) as an abuse brake. Results are stored server-side
(URL, verdict facts, timestamp) and shared between visitors: the second person
to check the same URL gets the cached result.

## Probes are inert by design

The service never sends: session cookies, PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS fields,
file parts, oversized/stalling bodies, or any exploit payload. It only observes
banners, statuses, redirect behavior and Set-Cookie echo. Telemetry: the
probes identify as a scanner UA and are documented in the project's
detections/ notes for SOC filtering.
